rules.sentence: Asymptomatic pyuria and bacteriuria should not be treated unless the patient is exhibiting signs and/or symptoms of a UTI or sepsis.
Enterococcus is frequently cited as one of the three most likely etiologies of both uncomplicated and complicated UTI, especially healthcare-associated UTIs.
As commensals, vancomycin-resistant Enterococcusis commonly isolated from intra-abdominal and pelvic infections.
Intra-abdominal and pelvic abscesses are commonly associated with enterococcal bacteremia prompting antibiotic coverage of Enterococcus.
